2. XOR blend. Source finding (ogkm-580): NVKMS never programs anything XOR- or invert-like. All five of its cursor blend modes use MODE_BLEND (nvkms-evo3.c:6646-6702, nvkms-evo4.c:965-1019, nvkms-evo2.c:3194-3206), its only cursor format is A8R8G8B8, and no factor pair can invert. The semantics are therefore a stated definition: out = below XOR (src & 0x00ffffff), alpha and factors unused; the masked-colour reading is recorded as the alternative. The compose kernel is hand-written PTX with no FNV pin; flags bit 3 = XOR, one branch, parameter list unchanged. kf-disp gains the COMPOSE_* constants, an XOR plan in plan_cursor and compose_reference (the CPU reference). kf-cuda refuses unknown flag bits; kf-qemu pins the two flag sets equal and its bring-up GPU self-test gains an XOR pixel. An XOR cursor is composed in every mode and the host cursor stays hidden.

Host test of the same arithmetic: /workspace/kf-broker/crates/kf-disp/tests/compose_kernel.rs parses and runs the committed PTX text instruction by instruction, for every (CTA, thread), and compares byte for byte with compose_reference. Cases: pitch, block-linear, every blend, swap, XOR, a stride loop past 256 pixels, clipping; every load and store is bounds-checked.

3. QEMU console cursor (the coordinator's decision, recorded in V3_DISPLAY §8.13 as revisable by the owner). In hover with a CAP_CURSOR broker the console gets the guest cursor through dpy_cursor_define + dpy_mouse_set. Under grab, for XOR, or with the broker gone it gets the hidden cursor, but only if it was ever given one. Decided: without a broker the console stays composed, because QEMU cannot tell whether a viewer can draw a defined cursor (ui/vnc.c:992-1027). Logic in /workspace/kf-broker/crates/kf-broker/src/console.rs (GPU-free tests; pixels converted to straight 0xAARRGGBB). Glue: kf-qemu ffi_unsafe.rs gains Kf3Cursor, kf3_display_cursor and kf3_display_cursor_pixels (null, alignment and size checked); kf3.c gains kf3_console_cursor, called at gfx_update and after each broker pump. Ownership follows QEMU 10.2.4: dpy_cursor_define takes its own reference and kf3.c drops its own. KF3 ABI stays 12. kf3.c passes -fsyntax-only -Werror against qemu-10.2.4 with QEMU's own flags (gcc 15).

Cursor alpha: source reading cannot settle it. kf-disp's mapping is the head's own arithmetic for each mode; nvidia-drm defaults to PREMULT; the NVIDIA X driver that would choose straight alpha is closed. findings.where: crates/kf-broker/src/console.rs:95-110 (poll defines the image as soon as share.mode() reads Hover); qemu/hw/misc/kf3/kf3.c:1050-1055 (kf3_broker_pump calls only kf3_console_cursor) vs kf3.c:771-781 (the frame is picked up only in kf3_gfx_update)
findings.issue: The 'never two cursors' rule breaks for a short time on grab->hover, and on Off->hover when a broker connects. The relay sets Hover while it handles EV_GRAB, and the pump then runs kf3_console_cursor straight away, so dpy_cursor_define puts the guest image on the console at once. The console surface still holds the last frame, which has the cursor composed into it. It gets a cursor-free frame only after the worker recomposes and the console's next gfx_update takes it, and VNC's refresh backs off to 3 s on an idle screen (§8.13 cites this itself). Until then a cursor-capable VNC viewer shows two cursors: the defined one and the stale composed one. The box only graded 'after ungrab: 0 changed pixels' after a sleep, which cannot see this window. The opposite transition (hover->grab, or XOR) leaves zero cursors for the same window.
findings.fix: Tie the console's define to the frame the console actually shows. The worker publishes cursor_in_frame with each frame serial. ConsoleCursor defines the image only after kf3_gfx_update has taken a frame with the bit clear, and defines the hidden cursor when it takes a frame with the bit set. At minimum, have kf3_broker_pump also take a pending frame (the kf3_gfx_update frame path) before it calls kf3_console_cursor. Add a GPU-free test: grab->hover must not define the image while the shown frame still has the cursor composed.

findings.where: crates/kf-broker/src/console.rs:145-170 (pixels converted to STRAIGHT alpha); QEMU 10.2.4 ui/vnc.c:1001-1010 (the alpha cursor goes on the wire as c->data unchanged); scripts/bench/display/vnc_cursor.py:43-49,114 (the grader premultiplies what it receives); docs/design/V3_DISPLAY.md:2521 and the §8.13 STATUS
findings.issue: QEMU's frontends disagree on the QEMUCursor alpha convention. SDL (ui/sdl2.c:763) and GTK (ui/gtk.c:480) read the words as straight alpha. VNC's -314 'Cursor With Alpha' encoding sends c->data verbatim, and that encoding is premultiplied on the wire (rfbproto; TigerVNC's CMsgReader::readSetCursorWithAlpha un-premultiplies what it receives — I recall this but did not verify it locally). The coordinator's decision targets VNC viewers. A spec-following VNC client would un-premultiply kayfabe's straight words, so the arrow's 163 partly transparent pixels and the crosshair's 150 come out too bright or wrap around. The box grade does not catch this: vnc_cursor.py assumes straight and premultiplies before hashing, so 'the VNC copy matches the host pixel for pixel' shows the transport round-trips under kayfabe's own assumption, not what a VNC client draws. The §8.12 alpha conclusion still holds (it needs only kayfabe's image to equal the host's), but the §8.13 claim that VNC shows the cursor correctly is unverified for semi-transparent pixels.
findings.fix: Check the rfbproto -314 text and TigerVNC's reader. Record the split in §8.13: SDL/GTK expect straight alpha, VNC -314 expects premultiplied, and one QEMUCursor cannot satisfy both, so pick the frontend the decision serves (VNC) or say what each one shows. Grade with a real viewer (a TigerVNC vncviewer screenshot of an anti-aliased edge), or make vnc_cursor.py take the wire as premultiplied and report the mismatch, instead of hashing under kayfabe's own convention.

findings.where: crates/kf-broker/src/console.rs:124-131 (dpy_mouse_set with on=false when hiding); qemu/hw/misc/kf3/kf3.c:1006-1008 then 1054 then 760; QEMU ui/gtk.c:447-466; ui/input.c:101-122; docs/design/V3_DISPLAY.md:2804
findings.issue: At hover->grab, poll() sends mouse=(last x, last y, off). kf3_broker_pump has already run KF3_BROKER_GRAB -> kf3_broker_set_relative(true), so the call reaches QEMU with a relative device active. GTK's gd_mouse_set warps the host pointer whenever qemu_input_is_absolute(con) is false. That happens when the tablet is not bound to this console: qemu_input_find_handler prefers bound handlers, and the lane binds its tablet with display=kf0, which hides the problem there. With -display gtk and an unbound tablet, every broker grab therefore warps the host pointer into QEMU's window, while the broker holds the grab. §8.13 says GTK 'ignores it under an absolute pointer', but the grab is exactly what makes input relative.
findings.fix: Send dpy_mouse_set only in Hover with an image defined (on=true). When hiding, define the hidden cursor and make no mouse call: it has no consumer then. Correct the §8.13 sentence.

findings.issue: poll() records told, latched and mouse before C has done anything. kf3_console_cursor can still return early: a size or hot-spot bound, cursor_alloc returning NULL, or kf3_display_cursor_pixels returning -1. That early return also skips the MOUSE part. Rust then believes the image is defined and never retries, so the console can keep a stale cursor, possibly next to a composed one, until the image digest changes. The paths are close to unreachable today, but the divergence is silent.
findings.fix: Have C report the outcome, e.g. a kf3_display_cursor_done(h, ok) that rolls back told and mouse on failure. Or apply the mouse even when the define fails, and reset told to force a re-define on the next poll.

findings.where: crates/kf-broker/src/conn.rs:1236-1241 (Linear and Implicit commits counted in c.dmabuf) vs conn.rs:1974-1990 (format() reclaims frames on x=0 and leaves the Ack unchanged)
findings.issue: A dma-buf commit that the broker explicitly refused at its format gate (EV_FORMAT x=0, then reclaimed) still counts toward the silent-drop detector. Before the class's first RELEASE on a connection, three such drops in ≥1 s trip a 5–60 s back-off, and the log blames an unreadable /proc/self/fdinfo. The drops are easy to get: the relay counts an Asked verdict as yes, so the first frame of each connection races its own query. brkF1's conn2 had two LINEAR gate drops. On an X11 dma-buf tier the F_SHM fallback is refused silently (nb_session_x11.c: accept_shm is set only in the shm tier), so a false trip can freeze the picture.
findings.fix: When format() reclaims a frame for an x=0, remove that commit from the matching Ack (decrement unacked, and clear unacked_since at 0). Or count only commits under a pair whose verdict is Yes. Add a relay_machine case: three gate drops answered by x=0 must not trip.

findings.issue: The four new counters are missing from the status fragment the box lane collects: dmabuf_trips, carrier_refused, carrier_unchecked and formats_unasked. The code calls carrier_refused 'a kayfabe defect whenever it is not zero'. As a result, §8.15's 'RUN ON A BOX' for rows 4 and 5 has no counter evidence that nothing was refused, unchecked or tripped on hardware. The only signal is the bounded log lines, and the committed excerpts do not show them.
findings.fix: Add the four counters to Relay::status(), and have broker_lane.sh grade carrier_refused=0 and dmabuf_trips=0 on the GPU-copy runs.

findings.issue: Two log lines can say something false. (a) attach() calls attach_cmd before the descriptor check, so a frame refused for its descriptor has already logged 'frames go as a LINEAR dma-buf' (rung_logged is set, so the line never repeats) and used up a seq. (b) The finding the box run left unfixed: on the first connection HELLO logs 'no /dev/udmabuf here, so frames go as shared memory only' even though udmabuf is present (seen in brkF1 excerpt line 10).
findings.fix: Run the descriptor check (ring_fd + carried) before attach_cmd, or set rung_logged only after the send succeeds. In hello(), judge udmabuf by whether the device opened /dev/udmabuf, not by whether a slot already holds a dma-buf.

findings.issue: 'Rung 0 carried every frame and each came back released' overstates the evidence. brkF2 has sent=7263 against gpucopy=7262, because each connection's first frame went LINEAR and was dropped at the format gate. brkF1's conn2 dropped two LINEAR frames, then logged 'frames go as shared memory (F_SHM)' (run_brkF1_qemu_excerpt.log:173) against an X11 dma-buf-tier broker that refuses F_SHM. The evidence README states this correctly; the design doc does not.
findings.fix: Use the README's wording: the first frame(s) of each connection went LINEAR (dropped at the gate) or F_SHM, then every frame was a block-linear GPU copy and was released.

findings.where: qemu/hw/misc/kf3/kf3.c:1051-1055 (kf3_broker_pump calls kf3_console_cursor after every pump); crates/kf-broker/src/console.rs:99-113 (a Hidden-to-Image switch redefines the whole image); crates/kf-broker/src/conn.rs:1739-1745 (grab is taken from F_GRABBED on every packet) and :2205 (the mode is set once per ready); kf3.c:738-757
findings.issue: The broker can make QEMU's main thread do a lot of work for very little input. Nothing paces the console's cursor defines. A hostile broker can flip F_GRABBED between socket reads, which flips the mode between Hover and Grabbed once per pump. Each return to Hover redefines the full cursor: cursor_alloc of up to 256x256x4 = 256 KiB, a 64K-pixel straight-alpha conversion with divides (console.rs:158-167), then dpy_cursor_define. That call builds VNC's mono mask (ui/vnc.c:1035-1038) and writes 256 KiB to every alpha-cursor VNC client (vnc.c:1001-1009), or creates a GdkCursor or SDL cursor. All of this runs under the BQL, so 32-byte packets can saturate the main loop that vCPU exits and timers depend on. VNC viewers also get disconnected once QEMU's output throttle trips (vnc.c:1676-1683). Before this change a grab flip cost only a GPU recompose on the worker thread, which runs one at a time. The guest-side rate is bounded by the worker pass and is the same class as virtio-gpu; the broker-side rate is not bounded at all.
findings.fix: Pace console DEFINEs inside ConsoleCursor::poll. Allow at most one DEFINE per about 16 ms (the broker already paces its own uploads at 8 ms), let the latest state win, and apply a pending define at the next gfx_update or pump. Alternatively, debounce mode changes for the console so a Hover/Grabbed flip only counts once it has been stable for N ms. Also cache the converted pixel words for the latched digest so a return to Hover does not redo the conversion. Add a relay_machine test: a broker alternating F_GRABBED 1000 times gives at most a bounded number of console defines.

findings.where: crates/kf-broker/src/console.rs:137-169 (pixels() turns the premultiplied image into STRAIGHT alpha); scripts/bench/display/vnc_cursor.py:16-20,50-58,122 (the grader assumes straight alpha on the wire)
findings.issue: The coordinator chose this path so VNC clients show the guest cursor as a real pointer, but VNC gets the wrong alpha convention. RFB's Cursor With Alpha pseudo-encoding (-314) says 'Alpha is pre-multiplied for each colour channel' (rfbproto.rst, 'Cursor With Alpha Pseudo-encoding'). QEMU writes QEMUCursor.data to the wire unchanged (ui/vnc.c:1009). kf3 converts to straight alpha, citing only SDL and GTK (console.rs:138-141). A viewer that follows the spec therefore reads every semi-transparent pixel as c*255/a and composites it brighter than intended, often with a channel above alpha, so anti-aliased edges glow or go out of range. The box evidence cannot see this. vnc_cursor.py premultiplies whatever it receives before hashing, and its --selftest fake QEMU sends straight words, so the 'exact digest match' (0xf6108d49685ef58f) only shows that premultiplied to straight to premultiplied round-trips. The console bite-mutation 'premultiplied pixels passed through -> 1 red' locks in the same assumption.
findings.fix: Pass the premultiplied words through unchanged. The CursorImage is already premultiplied ARGB; this matches the -314 spec and what QEMU's virtio-gpu path effectively hands VNC. Record in V3_DISPLAY §8.13 that GTK/SDL then get slightly darker edges, the same as QEMU with virtio-gpu, or make that tradeoff an owner question. Flip the console unit test and its bite-mutation. Fix vnc_cursor.py to treat the wire as premultiplied, and add a partially transparent pixel to its selftest as a known-positive. Re-grade on the arrow cursor, which has 62 partially transparent pixels.

findings.where: crates/kf-qemu/src/display.rs:2676-2698 (host_cursor_want: one eprintln per change of the composition word)
findings.issue: A hostile guest can grow the host log without bound. host_cursor_want runs on every composed frame while a CAP_CURSOR broker is connected (display.rs:2827-2829). The new line is logged 'once per change' of a word the guest programs itself (HEAD_SET_CONTROL_CURSOR_COMPOSITION: k1, factors, mode). If guest root alternates two words each frame, the host gets roughly 300 bytes per frame at 60-144 Hz, indefinitely: several GB a day in QEMU's stderr, plus an alpha census each time. Every neighbouring log is rate-limited (n <= 4 || n % 256 == 0, display.rs:2722; loud() in conn.rs:603).
findings.fix: Count these lines and apply the same rule as the neighbouring logs (for example the first 8 changes, then every 256th), or log only the first change per word value seen. Keep cursor_comp so an unchanged word stays silent.

findings.issue: The verdict table evicts the wrong rows first: when full, it drops its oldest row that is not a 'no' before any volunteered 'no'. A broker that sends unasked EV_FORMAT x=0 for 16 or more fresh pairs therefore pushes out the relay's own Asked and Yes rows (for example the GPU-copy pair). Each such cycle costs one packet. The relay then re-sends QUERY on the next frame and logs 'the display CAN show ...' unconditionally (was.is_some() skips loud(), :1957), and native_allowed and want_vram flap frame by frame. It is bounded by the frame rate, but a hostile broker gets a per-frame log line and churn. Volunteered rows for pairs the relay never sends, such as X11's AR24 twins, are worth the least, yet they are kept ahead of the relay's own questions.
findings.fix: Evict unasked rows first (any verdict), then asked rows that are not 'no', then asked 'no's. The relay asks at most about 3 pairs, so its own rows can never be pushed out by volunteered ones. Add a relay_machine test: 32 unasked x=0 packets leave a recorded Yes for the GPU-copy pair intact.

findings.issue: Guest root can warp the host pointer through QEMU's GTK console. The console's MOUSE position comes from guest-programmed head registers. QEMU's GTK frontend warps the real host pointer to those coordinates whenever the console's input is relative (ui/gtk.c:447-467: gdk_window_get_root_coords + gdk_device_warp; the root coordinates are not clamped to the window). Guest root can make input relative by leaving the virtio-tablet inactive, since the bench also attaches virtio-mouse-pci. With a GTK console next to a hovering broker, the guest could then yank the host pointer across the host screen. kayfabe never called dpy_mouse_set before this change. Hover is meaningless without absolute input, so dropping MOUSE in relative mode loses nothing.
findings.fix: In kf3_console_cursor, call dpy_mouse_set only when qemu_input_is_absolute(s->con) (or skip MOUSE entirely: VNC ignores it, vnc.c:986-990, and SDL warps only under its own grab). Note the rule in §8.13.

findings.issue: The 'no cursor' sentinel collides with a real position. A cursor image top-left of (-1,-1) packs to 0xFFFFFFFF | 0xFFFFFFFF<<32 == u64::MAX and reads back as None, so the console keeps the stale position. This happens with the crosshair (derived hot spot 11,11) at guest pointer (10,10).
findings.fix: Make the sentinel unreachable. Clamp x and y to ±(1<<30) before packing (coordinates beyond that mean nothing), or store a separate valid bit.

findings.where: crates/kf-broker/src/conn.rs:1185-1201 (attach: carrier refusal) with choose() :944-968 and attach_cmd :1108,1127; crates/kf-linux-raw/src/host_fd_unsafe.rs:339-367
findings.issue: A descriptor refusal on the chosen rung refuses the frame without trying another rung. If the GPU-copy VRAM descriptor ever classified as Neither, choose() would pick Native on every frame. No commit would happen, so the native detector would never trip, and the broker display would stay black permanently (logged, rate-limited). attach_cmd also advances seq and logs 'frames go as ...' before the check, so the log claims a rung that sent nothing. Separately, every ATTACH of a dma-buf now opens and reads /proc/self/fdinfo on QEMU's main thread while holding the relay Mutex. It does not block, but it is a per-frame filesystem open for descriptors that are memfds or dma-bufs by construction.
findings.fix: On a carrier refusal, withdraw or back off that rung (for example through the same Ack back-off, or by marking that slot kind withdrawn) so the next frame falls back to the host rungs. Run the carrier check before attach_cmd's seq and rung_logged side effects. Cache the classification per descriptor identity (sent_id or inode), which is already tracked, so /proc is read once per backing, not once per frame.

findings.issue: The C glue has three hardening gaps. (a) cursor_builtin_hidden() can return NULL (ui/cursor.c:22-44), and dpy_cursor_define(con, NULL) then dereferences it in cursor_ref (ui/console.c:968). The cursor_alloc branch checks for NULL; this one does not. (b) ConsoleCursor::poll records told and latched before C applies the define. If any C-side check returns early, Rust believes the console holds the image until the image changes, and the early return also skips that poll's MOUSE, which Rust has already marked as sent. (c) kf3_display_cursor writes *out after a null check only; its sibling kf3_display_cursor_pixels also checks is_aligned (§R: validate at the _unsafe boundary). The C caller passes an aligned stack struct, so this is consistency, not a live bug.
findings.fix: (a) Add `if (!qc) return;` before dpy_cursor_define. (b) In the C, do not skip MOUSE when DEFINE fails, and add a kf3 entry (or a flag on the pixels call) that tells Rust to forget `told` after a failed define. (c) Add !out.is_aligned() to the guard in kf3_display_cursor (and kf3_display_frame) and count it in the ratchet comment.

R1.1 (two cursors briefly after ungrab or a broker connect): the console's cursor now follows the frame the console actually shows. New kf_broker::FrameCursors and ShownFrame: the worker marks each frame it publishes with whether the cursor is composed in (Inflight.cursor -> FrameView.cursor), and ConsoleShare::take records it. ConsoleCursor::poll no longer gives the console a cursor while the shown frame already has one composed. In hover it defines the image only once a frame without the composed cursor is shown. Under grab or XOR it keeps the image it already defined until a frame carrying the cursor is shown, so there is never zero cursors either. kf3_gfx_update now takes its frame first and polls the cursor after (new kf3_console_frame).

R1.2 / R2.2 (VNC alpha convention): QEMUCursor pixels are now passed through premultiplied. I checked the claim: rfbproto.rst says encoding -314 is 'pre-multiplied for each colour channel', and TigerVNC's CMsgReader::readSetCursorWithAlpha un-premultiplies (both fetched 2026-10-04). Cost: SDL and GTK show a slightly darker edge, the same as QEMU's own virtio-gpu (hw/display/virtio-gpu.c:74 memcpy). This is recorded in §8.13. vnc_cursor.py now hashes the wire as received and counts wire_above_alpha; its selftest includes a straight word as a known-positive.

R1.3 / R2.5 (host pointer warps): Rust emits MOUSE only in hover, for an image the console holds, always with on=1. kf3.c calls dpy_mouse_set only when qemu_input_is_absolute(s->con), because GTK's gd_mouse_set warps the host pointer on relative input. The wrong GTK sentence in §8.13 is corrected in place.

R1.4 / R2.8b (Rust believed a define happened when C dropped it): new kf3_display_cursor_done(h, applied), a safe extern fn on the unmerged ABI 12 surface. ConsoleCursor::done takes back whatever QEMU did not apply, so it is handed out again (still paced). R2.8a: cursor_builtin_hidden returning NULL is now checked. R2.8c: kf3_display_cursor and kf3_display_frame now refuse a misaligned pointer at the boundary.

R2.1 (hostile broker flooding defines): at most one DEFINE per DEFINE_MIN_MS = 16 ms, and the newest state wins at the first poll after that. Combined with the frame tie, a broker flipping F_GRABBED can no longer force a define per packet. Caching converted pixels is moot: the words are now copied straight, with no division.
R1.5: a dma-buf commit refused by name (EV_FORMAT x=0 reclaiming it) is removed from the silent-drop detector's count (Held.committed, Ack::uncount).

R1.6: the status fragment now carries dmabuf_trips, carrier_refused, carrier_unchecked and formats_unasked. broker_lane.sh prints BRK_COUNTER_GRADE: PASS or FAIL on a GPU-copy run, UNMEASURED when the counters are missing, never zero by default. I exercised it on synthetic status lines.

R1.7 / R2.7 (descriptor check): the check now runs before a seq is spent or a rung is logged; the rung line is logged only after the ATTACH went. A refused dma-buf rung (GPU copy or host dma-buf) backs off for the connection through the same Ack back-off, and the same frame takes the next rung. A frame is refused, by name, only when its F_SHM memfd fails or no other rung holds it ('no other rung holds it'). Each descriptor is checked once per backing, cached by its id (carrier_ok, counted by carrier_checks). The HELLO line no longer claims 'no /dev/udmabuf' before any frame slot is installed.
R2.4: the verdict table now evicts rows the broker volunteered (any verdict) first, then the relay's own non-'no' rows, and its own 'no' rows last.

R2.3: the composition-word log line is bounded: the first 8 changes, then every 256th (kf_disp::scanout::CompositionLog), with the change number in the line. R2.6: the cursor point's 'none' value no longer collides with (-1, -1) (kf_broker::CursorPoint: 31-bit fields plus a valid bit).
